mainEntity.name: Do I need to convert units before entering my measurements?

acceptedAnswer.text: No — just make sure both waist and height are in the same unit (both inches or both centimetres), since the ratio itself is unitless as long as they match.

mainEntity.name: Is waist-to-height ratio better than BMI?

acceptedAnswer.text: They measure different things. Research suggests waist-to-height ratio is a better indicator of central fat and related cardiometabolic risk, but most health professionals — including NICE — view the two as complementary rather than one replacing the other.

mainEntity.name: Where exactly should I measure my waist?

acceptedAnswer.text: Find the bottom of your lowest rib and the top of your hip bone, and measure around your body midway between them, keeping the tape level and snug but not compressing the skin. Breathe out normally before reading the tape.
NICE classes 0.4 to 0.49 as healthy central adiposity for adults. From 0.5 health risks are increased, and from 0.6 they are further increased.
